Overall, the pacing of the story feels measured, calm, and reflective of the slow, steady rhythm of a river ferry crossing in the fog. The narrative mostly unfolds in real-time (scene time), matching the few minutes it takes to cross the river. Time is briefly compressed in the opening paragraph and in the descriptions of the passengers to summarize decades of Ilse's career and her past observations of the young woman. Conversely, time is gently stretched when the phone rings midway across the river; by detailing the reactions of the dog, the passengers, and Ilse's physical tension over three paragraphs, the author effectively heightens the quiet suspense and emotional weight of the unanswered call before smoothly compressing the final stretch of the crossing ("Nach einer Weile..." / "After a while..."). (Note: While there are a few minor continuity hiccups regarding when the ferry actually leaves the dock and where the phone is located, the temporal pacing itself is very well balanced.)
